body:
packages/fleet/lib/complete.mjs's completeTicketOnIntegration captures the pre-completion ledger snapshot (priorManifest) WITHOUT holding the manifest ledger lock. The ticket lock it does hold does not exclude an independent gate-manifest recorder writing to the same ledger file concurrently.

Failure scenario: Fleet snapshots the ledger (priorManifest = A). A concurrent recorder appends signed entry B and releases the ledger lock. TicketService.apply then appends completion entry C. A pre-commit hook rejects the commit. The rollback path captures afterManifest right after its own append (A+B+C) and, in the failed-commit branch, compares the CURRENT file against afterManifest — if they still match (no THIRD write landed since), it calls restoreFile(manifestAbs, priorManifest), replacing A+B+C with the pre-snapshot A. This silently deletes B — another writer's genuinely-recorded, signed evidence — even though the "stillOurTail" check was specifically designed to detect a concurrent append and refuse to blindly restore over one. The check runs too late: it only detects an append that happened AFTER Fleet's own write (afterManifest), never one that happened in the snapshot-to-write window (between priorManifest and afterManifest), because that concurrent write B ends up folded into afterManifest itself and looks like part of Fleet's own change.

This exact pattern predates T-MANIFEST-FOREST (segments): it already existed for the root-only manifest.jsonl before any segment writer existed. Surfaced during T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3's adversarial review (PR #411) while auditing the newly-segment-aware version of this same function, but the underlying lock-timing gap is orthogonal to segments and needs its own fix, not a segment-specific patch.

Acceptance criteria:
1. completeTicketOnIntegration's priorManifest snapshot and the eventual TicketService.apply write happen inside one manifest-ledger-lock critical section (or an equivalent mechanism, e.g. the writer returning an exact append token that can be used to remove only its own bytes rather than diffing before/after snapshots). A concurrent recorder's append between the snapshot and the write must never be silently erased by a subsequent rollback. Verify: node --test packages/fleet/test/complete.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='concurrent'
2. Add a regression test that holds the manifest ledger lock, appends a concurrent entry during the window between Fleet's snapshot and its own write, releases the lock, then forces a failed commit — asserting the concurrent entry survives the rollback. Verify: node --test packages/fleet/test/complete.test.mjs
3. Existing fleet test suite stays green. Verify: node --test packages/fleet/test/*.test.mjs
title: Fleet's completion rollback can erase a concurrent recorder's evidence (pre-existing race, predates T-MANIFEST-FOREST)
